sections.title: Project 1: Live Email Drafter (LangChain)
sections.body:
### Overview

The user pastes an incoming email and a one-line intent ("Agree to send rollback plan by Friday; no customer downtime expected"). The agent streams a drafted reply to the terminal token-by-token using `rich.live` to re-render a markdown pane as tokens arrive. The whole draft appears in 5-10 seconds, but because the user sees it forming they perceive it as instant.

Key APIs:

- `ChatOpenAI(streaming=True)` — enables token streaming on the model. Required for `.stream()` on the chain to actually yield per-token chunks.
- `chain.stream({...})` — LCEL primitive. Returns an iterator of `AIMessageChunk` objects, each carrying a few tokens.
- `rich.live.Live(renderable, refresh_per_second=15)` — re-renders a `rich` renderable up to 15 times per second. We update it on every chunk.
- `rich.markdown.Markdown` — renders markdown-formatted text in the terminal with proper styling.

### Full Code

```python
"""Day 14 Project 1: Live Email Drafter (LangChain).

Streams a drafted email reply token-by-token to the terminal
using chain.stream() + rich.live for real-time rendering.
"""
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
from rich.console import Console
from rich.live import Live
from rich.markdown import Markdown
from rich.panel import Panel

load_dotenv()
console = Console()

# streaming=True is required for chain.stream() to yield per-token chunks
llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0.7, streaming=True)

prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(
    "You are an assistant drafting a professional email reply.\n\n"
    "Incoming email from {sender}:\n"
    "'''\n{incoming}\n'''\n\n"
    "User's intent: {intent}\n\n"
    "Draft a concise reply (max 150 words). Sign off as 'Alex'.\n\n"
    "Reply:"
)

chain = prompt | llm

def draft_live(sender: str, incoming: str, intent: str) -> str:
    """Stream the drafted email token-by-token with rich live rendering."""
    rendered = ""
    # Live re-renders its child up to refresh_per_second times per second
    with Live(Markdown(rendered), console=console, refresh_per_second=15) as live:
        for chunk in chain.stream({
            "sender": sender,
            "incoming": incoming,
            "intent": intent,
        }):
            token = chunk.content  # AIMessageChunk.content holds the delta
            rendered += token
            live.update(Markdown(rendered))
    return rendered

def main() -> None:
    incoming = (
        "Hi Alex, we reviewed your team's proposal for the API migration. "
        "The scope looks reasonable but we need clarity on the rollback plan "
        "and timeline. Can you send details by EOD Friday? Also, will there "
        "be downtime for our customers?\n\n— Priya, VP Engineering"
    )
    intent = "Agree to send rollback plan by Friday; no customer downtime expected."

    console.rule("[bold cyan]Live Email Drafter[/]")
    console.print(f"[bold]From:[/] Priya <priya@acme.com>")
    console.print(f"[bold]Incoming:[/] {incoming[:80]}...")
    console.print(f"[bold]Intent:[/] {intent}")
    console.print()
    console.print("[bold green]Drafting reply...[/]")

    draft = draft_live("Priya <priya@acme.com>", incoming, intent)

    console.print()
    console.rule("[bold yellow]Final draft[/]")
    console.print(Panel(draft, title="Reply to Priya"))

    # Show token count for sanity
    console.print(f"\n[dim]Draft length: {len(draft)} chars, ~{len(draft.split())} words[/]")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### Walkthrough

**Model construction (line 14).** `streaming=True` is the critical flag. Without it, `chain.stream()` will still yield chunks, but each chunk is the entire response — defeating the purpose. With it, the OpenAI client uses Server-Sent Events and yields tokens as they arrive from the model.

**Chain construction (lines 24-25).** Standard LCEL: `prompt | llm`. We intentionally omit the output parser — we want raw `AIMessageChunk` objects so we can read `.content` per chunk. A `StrOutputParser` would also work and would yield strings directly, but the chunk type is the same.

**Live rendering (lines 28-40).** `Live(Markdown(""), refresh_per_second=15)` creates a context manager that re-renders its child up to 15 times per second. On each chunk we append to `rendered`, then call `live.update(Markdown(rendered))` to swap in the new renderable. The 15 fps cap matters — without it, you'd call `live.update` once per token (often 50+ times per second) and waste CPU on terminal I/O. `Markdown` renders headings, bold, lists, and code blocks inline in the terminal.

**Why `rich` and not `print`?** A naive `print(token, end="", flush=True)` works, but it can't do markdown rendering, can't show a panel around the text, and can't handle multi-line updates cleanly. `rich.live` solves all three. For a CLI tool, `rich` is the standard.

**The prompt.** The triple-quoted email template uses `'''` delimiters around the incoming email so the model can clearly see where the email ends and the intent begins. We cap at 150 words and require a signature — without caps, some models write 500-word essays.

### Expected Output

The terminal will show the email draft forming live, character by character. After streaming completes, you'll see:

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Live Email Drafter ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
From: Priya <priya@acme.com>
Incoming: Hi Alex, we reviewed your team's proposal for the API migration. The scope lo...
Intent: Agree to send rollback plan by Friday; no customer downtime expected.

Drafting reply...
[tokens stream live here, rendered as markdown]

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Final draft ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
┌─ Reply to Priya ─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Hi Priya,                                           │
│                                                     │
│ Thanks for the quick review. I'll send the rollback │
│ plan with step-by-step procedures and verification  │
│ checks by EOD Friday. There will be no customer     │
│ downtime — we're deploying behind a feature flag    │
│ and can revert in under 5 minutes if needed.        │
│                                                     │
│ Best,                                               │
│ Alex                                                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Draft length: 312 chars, ~54 words
```

sections.title: Project 2: Real-time Meeting Summarizer (Pydantic AI)
sections.body:
### Overview

A meeting summarizer that takes a long transcript and produces a structured result (`summary`, `action_items`, `risks`, `decisions`). The interesting part isn't the output — it's that you can watch every step of the agent loop as it happens via `agent.iter()`.

`agent.iter()` is an async context manager that yields nodes from the agent's internal execution graph. Each node represents one step: receiving the user prompt, sending a model request, processing tool calls, producing the final result. This is the developer-facing streaming API — it lets you build progress UIs, log telemetry, or react to tool calls in real time.

Key APIs:

- `agent.iter(prompt)` — async context manager yielding graph nodes.
- `agent.is_model_request_node(node)` / `agent.is_call_tools_node(node)` — type predicates for the two interesting node types.
- `run.result` — the final `RunResult` after the loop completes; `.output` is the typed result.
- `pydantic.BaseModel` as `result_type` — the agent returns a structured, validated object.

### Full Code

```python
"""Day 14 Project 2: Real-time Meeting Summarizer (Pydantic AI).

Uses agent.iter() to stream every event in the agent loop to the
terminal as it happens, then renders the structured final result.
"""
from typing import List

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from pydantic_ai import Agent
from rich.console import Console
from rich.live import Live
from rich.panel import Panel

load_dotenv()
console = Console()

# Sample meeting transcript (truncated for brevity; use a real one in practice)
TRANSCRIPT = """\
Meeting: Q3 Planning Sync — 2024-09-15
Attendees: Alex (Eng), Priya (VP Eng), Sam (Product), Jordan (Design)

Alex: Let's start with Q3 priorities. Priya, what's the board saying?
Priya: Board wants APAC expansion and lower churn. Both are non-negotiable.
Sam: For APAC, we need localized pricing and a Sydney datacenter.
Alex: Sydney DC is 6 weeks of work. Can we start next sprint?
Priya: Approved. Alex, you own the DC. Target go-live: Nov 1.
Sam: For churn, onboarding v2 launches Oct 15. That should help retention.
Jordan: I'll need 2 weeks for the localized UI strings. Start Sept 25.
Alex: I'll pull Maria in for infra. Action items?
Priya: Alex — Sydney DC by Nov 1. Sam — onboarding v2 by Oct 15.
Jordan — localized strings by Oct 9. I'll brief the board Friday.
Alex: Risks?
Priya: If Sydney DC slips, we lose the Q4 APAC launch window. Mitigation?
Alex: Hire a contractor for 4 weeks. Budget?
Priya: Approved up to $20k. Next sync in 2 weeks.
"""

class MeetingSummary(BaseModel):
    """Structured output returned by the summarizer."""
    summary: str = Field(description="2-3 sentence summary of the meeting")
    action_items: List[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="Each item: 'Owner — task — due date'")
    risks: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    decisions: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)

summarizer = Agent(
    "openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    result_type=MeetingSummary,
    system_prompt=(
        "You are a meeting summarizer. Read the transcript and produce "
        "a concise summary, action items (owner + task + due date), "
        "risks, and decisions. Be specific — cite owners by name. "
        "If a field has no entries, return an empty list."
    ),
)

async def summarize_live(transcript: str):
    """Run the agent and stream every step to a rich live panel."""
    events: list[str] = []

    with Live(Panel("\n".join(events) or "(starting...)", title="Agent Events"),
              console=console, refresh_per_second=10) as live:
        async with summarizer.iter(transcript) as run:
            async for node in run:
                # Each node is one step in the agent's execution graph
                cls_name = type(node).__name__
                if summarizer.is_model_request_node(node):
                    # Inspect the request being sent to the model
                    req = node.request
                    parts = getattr(req, "parts", [])
                    events.append(
                        f"[yellow]>> ModelRequestNode[/] ({len(parts)} parts)")
                elif summarizer.is_call_tools_node(node):
                    # The model responded — handle tool calls or finalize result
                    events.append(
                        "[magenta]>> CallToolsNode[/] (tools or final result)")
                else:
                    events.append(f"[cyan]>> {cls_name}[/]")
                # Keep the panel to the last 8 events for readability
                live.update(Panel("\n".join(events[-8:]), title="Agent Events"))

        return run.result

async def main() -> None:
    console.rule("[bold cyan]Real-time Meeting Summarizer[/]")
    console.print(f"[dim]Transcript: {len(TRANSCRIPT)} chars. "
                  f"Streaming agent events...[/]\n")

    result = await summarize_live(TRANSCRIPT)
    data: MeetingSummary = result.output

    console.rule("[bold yellow]Final structured output[/]")
    console.print(Panel(data.summary, title="Summary"))
    console.print(Panel(
        "\n".join(f"- {a}" for a in data.action_items) or "(none)",
        title="Action Items"))
    console.print(Panel(
        "\n".join(f"- {r}" for r in data.risks) or "(none)",
        title="Risks"))
    console.print(Panel(
        "\n".join(f"- {d}" for d in data.decisions) or "(none)",
        title="Decisions"))
    console.print(f"\n[dim]Tokens used: {result.usage()}[/]")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import asyncio
    asyncio.run(main())
```

### Walkthrough

**Transcript (lines 17-38).** A realistic Q3 planning sync. Notice it contains all four pieces of information we want extracted: a summary (the whole meeting), action items (with owners and dates), risks (Sydney DC slip), and decisions (contractor hire, $20k budget). Real transcripts are messier; consider pre-cleaning with a separate LLM call if quality matters.

**Structured result type (lines 41-52).** `MeetingSummary` is a Pydantic `BaseModel` with `Field` descriptions. Pydantic AI uses these descriptions to instruct the model on how to fill each field. The model's response is parsed and validated — if it returns malformed JSON or missing fields, Pydantic AI retries automatically (up to `model_settings={"max_retries": 1}` default).

**Agent (lines 55-63).** `result_type=MeetingSummary` is the key argument. It tells Pydantic AI to expect a structured output and to validate it. Under the hood, this becomes a function-calling schema for OpenAI or a JSON-schema response format for other providers.

**Event streaming (lines 66-89).** `summarizer.iter(transcript)` is an async context manager that returns an `AgentRun`. Iterating it yields nodes — one per step in the agent's execution graph. The two predicates `is_model_request_node` and `is_call_tools_node` are how you identify which kind of node you're looking at. We accumulate events into a list and re-render the last 8 in a `rich` panel.

**What you'll see in the panel.** A typical run yields: `UserPromptNode` (the transcript was received), `ModelRequestNode` (the request was sent), then `CallToolsNode` (the model's response is being handled — for a no-tool agent this is where the final result gets validated), then a second `ModelRequestNode` if a retry is needed, then END. Each step takes 1-3 seconds with `gpt-4o-mini`.

**Why this matters.** `iter()` is the foundation for production agent UIs. With it you can: show a spinner during model requests, render tool-call arguments as they form, prompt the user for approval before a destructive tool runs (Day 16), or stream tool output to a debug panel. Without `iter()`, you only get the final result — blind to what happened in between.

**Token streaming within `iter()`.** For token-level streaming inside a `ModelRequestNode`, Pydantic AI exposes `node.stream(run.ctx)` which returns an async iterator of partial deltas. This is more advanced and version-specific — for today we stick to event-level streaming. For pure token streaming, use `agent.run_stream()` (which returns an async iterator of text chunks directly).

### Expected Output

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Real-time Meeting Summarizer ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Transcript: 1014 chars. Streaming agent events...

┌─ Agent Events ──────────────────────────────┐
│ >> UserPromptNode                           │
│ >> ModelRequestNode (1 parts)               │
│ >> CallToolsNode (tools or final result)    │
│ >> ModelRequestNode (1 parts)               │
│ >> CallToolsNode (tools or final result)    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Final structured output ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
┌─ Summary ───────────────────────────────────┐
│ The team aligned on Q3 priorities: APAC     │
│ expansion via a Sydney datacenter and lower │
│ churn via onboarding v2. Owners and dates   │
│ were assigned for each initiative.          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─ Action Items ──────────────────────────────┐
│ - Alex — Sydney datacenter go-live — Nov 1  │
│ - Sam — onboarding v2 launch — Oct 15       │
│ - Jordan — localized UI strings — Oct 9     │
│ - Priya — brief board — Friday              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─ Risks ─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ - Sydney DC slip would lose Q4 APAC window  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─ Decisions ─────────────────────────────────┐
│ - Approved Sydney DC work starting next     │
│   sprint                                   │
│ - Approved $20k budget for 4-week           │
│   contractor to mitigate DC risk            │
│ - Onboarding v2 launches Oct 15             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Tokens used: Usage(requests=2, request_tokens=1240, response_tokens=215, total_tokens=1455)
```
